Spectral Space Transformation

Source: R/transfer.R
sst.Rd

Transfers spectra from one instrument (the slave) to another (the master) by spectral space transformation (SST; Du et al., 2011): the slave spectra are moved, in the space of the principal components shared by both instruments, by the difference between the instruments.

Usage

sst(x1, x2, ncomp = NULL, variance = 0.99)

Arguments

x1

The spectra of the transfer samples on the master instrument: a numeric matrix or data frame, one spectrum per row.

x2

The spectra of the same samples, in the same order, on the slave instrument.

ncomp

The number of principal components. By default, chosen from variance.

variance

The fraction of the variance explained, when ncomp is not given. Default is 0.99.

Value

An object of class specproc_transfer. Use predict() to transfer slave spectra.

Details

The transfer spectra of both instruments, centered by the mean of each instrument, are joined side by side, \([\textbf{X}_1\ \textbf{X}_2]\), and decomposed by a principal component analysis, \([\textbf{X}_1\ \textbf{X}_2] \approx \textbf{T} [\textbf{P}_1^T\ \textbf{P}_2^T]\): the same scores \(\textbf{T}\) describe a sample on both instruments, and the loadings \(\textbf{P}_1\) and \(\textbf{P}_2\) the spectra of each. A new slave spectrum gets the scores \(t = (x_2 - \bar{x}_2) (\textbf{P}_2^T)^{+}\) and is transferred by adding the difference of the instruments in that space: $$x_{2 \to 1} = \bar{x}_1 + (x_2 - \bar{x}_2) + t\,(\textbf{P}_1^T - \textbf{P}_2^T)$$ The part of the spectrum outside the shared components is kept unchanged, so SST corrects only the differences the transfer samples show.

By default, ncomp is the smallest number of components that explain the fraction variance of the variance of the joined spectra.

References

  • Du, W., Chen, Z.-P., Zhong, L.-J., Wang, S.-X., Yu, R.-Q., Nordon, A., Littlejohn, D., Holden, M. (2011). Maintaining the predictive abilities of multivariate calibration models by spectral space transformation. Analytica Chimica Acta, 690(1):64-70.

See also

ds(), pds(), slope_bias(), predict.specproc_transfer()

Author

Christian L. Goueguel

Examples

data(forageLIBS)
wl <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(names(forageLIBS)))
spectra <- as.matrix(forageLIBS[which(wl > 760 & wl < 780)])  # the K I lines
slave <- 0.8 * cbind(spectra[, -1], spectra[, ncol(spectra)]) + 50
transfer <- sst(spectra[1:30, ], slave[1:30, ])
transfer
#> Spectral space transformation (30 transfer samples, 245 wavelengths)
#> Components: 3 (99.12% of the variance)
transferred <- predict(transfer, slave[31:368, ])
mean(abs(transferred - spectra[31:368, ])) / mean(spectra)
#> [1] 0.02512886
